subproblem.title: Integration by parts on Ω for functions Lipschitz on Ω against C¹ fields compactly supported in Ω
subproblem.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ open, and let b : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ be C¹ with compact support and tsupport b ⊆ Ω. Then there is a Lebesgue-integrable g : ℝⁿ → ℝ (namely the divergence g = Σ_i ∂_i b_i) with the following property. For every L ≥ 0 and every f : ℝⁿ → ℝ that is L-Lipschitz on Ω: (a) w ↦ f(w)g(w) is Lebesgue integrable on Ω, and (b) ∫_Ω Df(w)(b(w)) dw = −∫_Ω f(w)g(w) dw. Here Df(w) = fderiv ℝ f w (the Fréchet derivative where it exists, 0 otherwise), and integrals are Bochner integrals for Lebesgue measure on ℝⁿ = Eucl n.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (Ω : Set (Eucl n)) (b : Eucl n → Eucl n), IsOpen Ω → ContDiff ℝ 1 b → HasCompactSupport b → tsupport b ⊆ Ω → ∃ g : Eucl n → ℝ, Integrable g (volume : Measure (Eucl n)) ∧ ∀ (L : ℝ≥0) (f : Eucl n → ℝ), LipschitzOnWith L f Ω → IntegrableOn (fun w => f w * g w) Ω (volume : Measure (Eucl n)) ∧ ∫ w in Ω, fderiv ℝ f w (b w) = -∫ w in Ω, f w * g w
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions. ℝⁿ = Eucl n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n). Lⁿ = volume, an additive Haar measure on the finite-dimensional space ℝⁿ. Dh(w) := fderiv ℝ h w, which is 0 where h is not differentiable. e_1, …, e_n is the standard orthonormal basis, e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1. For the field b, b_i := proj_i ∘ b, so b_i(x) is the i-th coordinate of b(x); here proj_i = EuclideanSpace.proj i is a continuous linear map, and b(x) = Σ_i b_i(x) e_i. All integrals are Bochner integrals for Lⁿ. Source: parent proof, steps 3–4; their argument uses only that b is C¹.
1. (Coordinates of b.) For each i, b_i = proj_i ∘ b is C¹, as the composition of the C¹ map b with a continuous linear map. Since proj_i(0) = 0, b_i has compact support (`HasCompactSupport.comp_left`) and tsupport b_i ⊆ tsupport b (`tsupport_comp_subset`). A C¹ function with compact support is globally Lipschitz: its derivative is continuous with compact support, hence bounded, and the mean value inequality applies (Mathlib `ContDiff.lipschitzWith_of_hasCompactSupport`, with n = 1 ≠ 0). Fix D_i ≥ 0 such that b_i is D_i-Lipschitz. Moreover b_i is differentiable everywhere and w ↦ Db_i(w) is continuous (`ContDiff.differentiable`, `ContDiff.continuous_fderiv`). Finally tsupport(Db_i) ⊆ tsupport b_i (`tsupport_fderiv_subset`), so Db_i(w) = 0 whenever w ∉ tsupport b.
2. (Definition of g.) Put g(w) := Σ_i Db_i(w)(e_i). Each summand is continuous in w, being the continuous map w ↦ Db_i(w) followed by evaluation at the fixed vector e_i; so g is continuous. By step 1, g(w) = 0 for w ∉ tsupport b. Since tsupport b is compact, g has compact support (`HasCompactSupport.intro`). Being continuous with compact support, g is Lⁿ-integrable on ℝⁿ (`Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport`). Also, since tsupport b ⊆ Ω, b(w) = 0 and g(w) = 0 for every w ∉ Ω. Now fix L ≥ 0 and f : ℝⁿ → ℝ that is L-Lipschitz on Ω. Note that g does not depend on L or f.
3. (McShane extension.) By McShane's extension theorem (Mathlib `LipschitzOnWith.extend_real`), there is F : ℝⁿ → ℝ which is L-Lipschitz on all of ℝⁿ and satisfies F = f on Ω. For w ∈ Ω, f and F agree on the neighbourhood Ω of w, so Df(w) = DF(w) (`Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq`).
4. (Claim (a).) F is continuous and g is continuous with compact support, so F·g is continuous with compact support. Hence F·g is integrable on ℝⁿ, and in particular on Ω. Since f·g = F·g on the measurable set Ω, f·g is integrable on Ω (`IntegrableOn.congr_fun`). This proves (a).
5. (Reduction to an identity on ℝⁿ.) By step 3, ∫_Ω Df(w)(b(w)) dw = ∫_Ω DF(w)(b(w)) dw (`setIntegral_congr_fun`). For w ∉ Ω we have DF(w)(b(w)) = DF(w)(0) = 0, so this equals ∫_{ℝⁿ} DF(w)(b(w)) dw (`setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero`). Likewise ∫_Ω f g = ∫_Ω F g = ∫_{ℝⁿ} F g, because F(w)g(w) = 0 for w ∉ Ω. Hence (b) is equivalent to the identity (★) ∫ DF(w)(b(w)) dw = −∫ F(w)g(w) dw over ℝⁿ.
6. (Expansion in coordinates.) For every w, b(w) = Σ_i b_i(w) e_i (expansion in the orthonormal basis `EuclideanSpace.basisFun`, `Basis.sum_repr`). By linearity, DF(w)(b(w)) = Σ_i DF(w)(e_i)·b_i(w). Each summand is integrable on ℝⁿ. Indeed, w ↦ DF(w)(e_i) is Borel measurable (`measurable_fderiv` followed by evaluation at e_i), and |DF(w)(e_i)| ≤ ‖DF(w)‖·|e_i| ≤ L for all w (`norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz`). Also b_i is continuous with compact support, hence integrable. A bounded measurable function times an integrable function is integrable (`Integrable.bdd_mul`). Therefore ∫ DF(w)(b(w)) dw = Σ_i ∫ DF(w)(e_i)·b_i(w) dw (`integral_finset_sum`).
7. (Rademacher and integration by parts in one coordinate.) Fix i. By Rademacher's theorem (Mathlib `LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt` for the Haar measure Lⁿ), F is differentiable at Lⁿ-a.e. w. At every such w, lineDeriv ℝ F w e_i = DF(w)(e_i) (`DifferentiableAt.lineDeriv_eq_fderiv`). Hence ∫ DF(w)(e_i)·b_i(w) dw = ∫ lineDeriv ℝ F w e_i · b_i(w) dw (`integral_congr_ae`). Apply the integration by parts formula for Lipschitz functions (Mathlib `LipschitzWith.integral_lineDeriv_mul_eq`) to F (L-Lipschitz), b_i (D_i-Lipschitz with compact support) and v = e_i; it applies because Lⁿ is an additive Haar measure on a finite-dimensional space. It gives ∫ lineDeriv ℝ F w e_i · b_i(w) dw = ∫ lineDeriv ℝ b_i w (−e_i) · F(w) dw. Since b_i is differentiable at every w, lineDeriv ℝ b_i w (−e_i) = Db_i(w)(−e_i) = −Db_i(w)(e_i). Therefore ∫ DF(w)(e_i)·b_i(w) dw = −∫ Db_i(w)(e_i)·F(w) dw (`integral_neg`).
8. (Summation.) For each i, w ↦ Db_i(w)(e_i)·F(w) is continuous and vanishes outside the compact set tsupport b (step 1), so it is integrable. Combining steps 6 and 7: ∫ DF(w)(b(w)) dw = Σ_i (−∫ Db_i(w)(e_i)·F(w) dw) = −∫ Σ_i Db_i(w)(e_i)·F(w) dw = −∫ F(w)g(w) dw (`integral_finset_sum`, `Finset.mul_sum`). This is (★), so by step 5 claim (b) holds. Together with step 2 (g is integrable) and step 4 (claim (a)), g has all the required properties, and it serves for every L and f. ∎
proof_key_steps: The coordinates b_i = proj_i ∘ b are C¹, have compact support and are Lipschitz (ContDiff.lipschitzWith_of_hasCompactSupport); Db_i = 0 outside tsupport b.
g := Σ_i Db_i(·)(e_i) is continuous with compact support inside tsupport b ⊆ Ω, hence integrable; g and b vanish off Ω.
McShane extension F of f: F is L-Lipschitz on ℝⁿ, F = f and DF = Df on Ω; f·g = F·g is integrable on Ω, and both integrals reduce to integrals over ℝⁿ with F.
DF(w)(b(w)) = Σ_i DF(w)(e_i)·b_i(w); each term is integrable because |DF(w)(e_i)| ≤ L and b_i is continuous with compact support.
By Rademacher, DF(w)(e_i) = lineDeriv ℝ F w e_i a.e.; LipschitzWith.integral_lineDeriv_mul_eq gives ∫ lineDeriv ℝ F w e_i · b_i = −∫ Db_i(w)(e_i)·F(w).
Summing over i gives ∫ DF(b) = −∫ F g, hence ∫_Ω Df(b) = −∫_Ω f g.

audit.reason: The existential contract correctly chooses one integrable g before quantifying over L and f. The proof constructs this witness as the divergence, verifies support and integrability, extends f, identifies derivatives locally, and applies Rademacher and Lipschitz integration by parts with the correct sign. Every finite-sum interchange is justified; C¹ regularity suffices.

subproblem.title: Lipschitz bound, in the field, for the pairing ∫_Ω Df(b) when f is C-Lipschitz on Ω
subproblem.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ open, C ≥ 0, and let f : ℝⁿ → ℝ be C-Lipschitz on Ω. Let b, b' : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ be Lebesgue integrable on Ω. Then |∫_Ω Df(w)(b(w)) dw − ∫_Ω Df(w)(b'(w)) dw| ≤ C·∫_Ω |b(w) − b'(w)| dw. Here Df(w) = fderiv ℝ f w (the Fréchet derivative where it exists, 0 otherwise), and all integrals are Bochner integrals for Lebesgue measure on ℝⁿ = Eucl n.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (Ω : Set (Eucl n)) (C : ℝ≥0) (f : Eucl n → ℝ), IsOpen Ω → LipschitzOnWith C f Ω → ∀ b b' : Eucl n → Eucl n, IntegrableOn b Ω (volume : Measure (Eucl n)) → IntegrableOn b' Ω (volume : Measure (Eucl n)) → |(∫ w in Ω, fderiv ℝ f w (b w)) - ∫ w in Ω, fderiv ℝ f w (b' w)| ≤ C * ∫ w in Ω, ‖b w - b' w‖
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions. ℝⁿ = Eucl n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) with Euclidean norm |·|. Lⁿ = volume and Lⁿ⌞Ω = volume.restrict Ω. Df(w) := fderiv ℝ f w is the Fréchet derivative of f at w if f is differentiable at w, and 0 otherwise. ‖A‖ is the operator norm of A ∈ L(ℝⁿ, ℝ). All integrals are Bochner integrals. Source: parent proof, steps 1–2.
1. (Pointwise derivative bound.) Let w ∈ Ω. Since Ω is open, it is a neighbourhood of w, and f is C-Lipschitz on Ω, so ‖Df(w)‖ ≤ C (Mathlib `norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitzOn ℝ (hΩ.mem_nhds hw) hf`). Directly: if f is differentiable at w, then for every v ∈ ℝⁿ, Df(w)v = lim_{t→0} (f(w+tv) − f(w))/t. For small |t| we have w + tv ∈ Ω, so |f(w+tv) − f(w)| ≤ C|t||v|, which gives |Df(w)v| ≤ C|v|. If f is not differentiable at w, then Df(w) = 0. Consequently, for every map v : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ and every w ∈ Ω, |Df(w)(v(w))| ≤ ‖Df(w)‖·|v(w)| ≤ C|v(w)|.
2. (Measurability.) The map w ↦ Df(w), from ℝⁿ to L(ℝⁿ, ℝ), is Borel measurable (Mathlib `measurable_fderiv ℝ f`). Its target is finite-dimensional, so it is also a.e. strongly measurable for Lⁿ⌞Ω. Let v be integrable on Ω; then v is Lⁿ⌞Ω-a.e. strongly measurable. The evaluation (A, s) ↦ A(s) is a continuous bilinear map L(ℝⁿ, ℝ) × ℝⁿ → ℝ. Hence w ↦ Df(w)(v(w)) is Lⁿ⌞Ω-a.e. strongly measurable (Mathlib `(ContinuousLinearMap.apply ℝ ℝ).aestronglyMeasurable_comp₂ hv.aestronglyMeasurable (measurable_fderiv ℝ f).aestronglyMeasurable`).
3. (Integrability.) Let v be integrable on Ω. By step 2, w ↦ Df(w)(v(w)) is Lⁿ⌞Ω-a.e. strongly measurable. By step 1 its absolute value is at most C|v(w)| for every w ∈ Ω, hence Lⁿ⌞Ω-a.e., since Ω is open and therefore measurable. As C|v| is integrable on Ω, w ↦ Df(w)(v(w)) is integrable on Ω (`Integrable.mono'`). In particular this holds for v = b and for v = b'.
4. (Linearity.) By step 3 and linearity of the integral (`integral_sub`), ∫_Ω Df(w)(b(w)) dw − ∫_Ω Df(w)(b'(w)) dw = ∫_Ω [Df(w)(b(w)) − Df(w)(b'(w))] dw. Since each Df(w) is linear, the integrand equals Df(w)(b(w) − b'(w)).
5. (Estimate.) The field b − b' is integrable on Ω, so C|b − b'| is integrable on Ω. By step 1 with v = b − b', |Df(w)(b(w) − b'(w))| ≤ C|b(w) − b'(w)| for all w ∈ Ω, hence Lⁿ⌞Ω-a.e. Therefore |∫_Ω Df(w)(b(w) − b'(w)) dw| ≤ ∫_Ω C|b(w) − b'(w)| dw = C·∫_Ω |b(w) − b'(w)| dw (`norm_integral_le_of_norm_le`, `integral_const_mul`). Together with step 4, this is the claimed inequality. ∎
proof_key_steps: For w ∈ Ω, Ω is a neighbourhood of w, so ‖Df(w)‖ ≤ C (norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitzOn); hence |Df(w)(v(w))| ≤ C|v(w)| on Ω.
w ↦ Df(w)(v(w)) is a.e. strongly measurable (measurable_fderiv composed with the continuous evaluation) and dominated on Ω by C|v|, so it is integrable on Ω for v = b and v = b'.
By linearity, ∫_Ω Df(b) − ∫_Ω Df(b') = ∫_Ω Df(w)(b(w) − b'(w)) dw.

The proof establishes derivative measurability, the bound on the open set, integrability of both pairings, justified integral subtraction, and the L¹ estimate. It is complete and independent of the parent and siblings.

subproblem.title: Density of C_c^∞ fields supported in Ω in L¹(Ω; ℝⁿ)
subproblem.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ open, and let c : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ be Lebesgue integrable on Ω. Then for every δ > 0 there is a C^∞ field b : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ with compact support and tsupport b ⊆ Ω such that ∫_Ω |c(w) − b(w)| dw < δ. Here C^∞ means ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) (smooth, not analytic), and the integral is for Lebesgue measure on ℝⁿ = Eucl n.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (Ω : Set (Eucl n)) (c : Eucl n → Eucl n), IsOpen Ω → IntegrableOn c Ω (volume : Measure (Eucl n)) → ∀ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ → ∃ b : Eucl n → Eucl n, ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) b ∧ HasCompactSupport b ∧ tsupport b ⊆ Ω ∧ ∫ w in Ω, ‖c w - b w‖ < δ
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions. ℝⁿ = Eucl n with Euclidean norm |·|; Lⁿ = volume; 1_A c := A.indicator c, the field equal to c on A and to 0 off A. Integrals are Bochner integrals for Lⁿ. Source: parent proof, step 6. Lean note: step 3 uses `MeasureTheory.MemLp.exist_eLpNorm_sub_le`, which lives in `Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Lp.SmoothApprox`. The frozen contract does not import that module, so add `import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Lp.SmoothApprox` to Submission.lean. The comparator does not restrict Submission imports, and the olean is in the shared package tree.
1. (Compact exhaustion of Ω.) Since Ω is open in the metric space ℝⁿ, there are closed sets F_0 ⊆ F_1 ⊆ ⋯, all contained in Ω, with ⋃_j F_j = Ω (Mathlib `IsOpen.exists_iUnion_isClosed`). Explicitly, F_j := {w : B(w, 1/(j+1)) ⊆ Ω} works. Its complement ⋃_{y ∉ Ω} B(y, 1/(j+1)) is open. Since w ∈ B(w, 1/(j+1)), F_j ⊆ Ω. The radii decrease, so the F_j increase. Every w ∈ Ω has a ball B(w, r) ⊆ Ω, so w ∈ F_j once 1/(j+1) ≤ r. Put K_j := F_j ∩ B̄(0, j). Each K_j is closed and bounded in ℝⁿ, hence compact; K_j ⊆ Ω; and K_i ⊆ K_j for i ≤ j. Moreover ⋃_j K_j = Ω: if w ∈ Ω, pick i with w ∈ F_i and a natural number j ≥ max(i, |w|); then w ∈ F_j by monotonicity and |w| ≤ j, so w ∈ K_j.
2. (Small tail.) |c| is integrable on Ω. The K_j are measurable and increasing with union Ω, so ∫_{K_j} |c| → ∫_Ω |c| as j → ∞ (`tendsto_setIntegral_of_monotone`). Fix j with |∫_{K_j} |c| − ∫_Ω |c|| < δ/2 and write K := K_j. Since K ⊆ Ω is measurable, ∫_{Ω∖K} |c| = ∫_Ω |c| − ∫_K |c| < δ/2 (`setIntegral_sdiff`).
3. (Smooth approximation of 1_K c on ℝⁿ.) The field 1_K c is Lⁿ-integrable on ℝⁿ, because c is integrable on K ⊆ Ω and K is measurable (`integrable_indicator_iff`); thus 1_K c ∈ L¹(ℝⁿ; ℝⁿ). Smooth compactly supported functions are dense in L^p for 1 ≤ p < ∞ (Mathlib `MeasureTheory.MemLp.exist_eLpNorm_sub_le` with p = 1; Lⁿ is finite on compacts). So there is b₀ : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ, C^∞ with compact support, with eLpNorm(1_K c − b₀, 1, Lⁿ) ≤ δ/2. For a.e.-strongly measurable h, eLpNorm(h, 1) = ∫⁻ |h| and ∫ |h| = (∫⁻ |h|).toReal (`eLpNorm_one_eq_lintegral_enorm`, `integral_norm_eq_lintegral_enorm`, `ENNReal.toReal_le_of_le_ofReal`). Hence ∫_{ℝⁿ} |1_K c(w) − b₀(w)| dw ≤ δ/2. Also b₀ is continuous with compact support, hence integrable.
4. (Smooth cutoff.) ℝⁿ is locally compact, K is compact, Ω is open and K ⊆ Ω. So there is a compact set L with K ⊆ interior L and L ⊆ Ω (`exists_compact_between`). Let W := interior L, an open set containing the closed set K. By the smooth Urysohn lemma (Mathlib `exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff` with smoothness ⊤ : ℕ∞, s = W, t = K), there is a C^∞ function χ : ℝⁿ → ℝ with values in [0, 1], support χ = W, and χ(x) = 1 exactly when x ∈ K. Then tsupport χ = closure W ⊆ L, because L is compact and hence closed. So χ has compact support, being supported in a closed subset of the compact set L, and tsupport χ ⊆ L ⊆ Ω.
5. (Definition of b.) Let b(w) := χ(w)·b₀(w). Then b is C^∞ as a product of C^∞ functions. Also tsupport b ⊆ tsupport χ ⊆ Ω (`tsupport_smul_subset_left`), and b has compact support because χ does (`HasCompactSupport.smul_right`). In particular b is continuous with compact support, hence Lⁿ-integrable.
6. (Pointwise estimate.) For every w ∈ ℝⁿ, |c(w) − b(w)| ≤ |1_{ℝⁿ∖K} c(w)| + |1_K c(w) − b₀(w)|. If w ∈ K, then χ(w) = 1, so c(w) − b(w) = c(w) − b₀(w) = 1_K c(w) − b₀(w), while 1_{ℝⁿ∖K} c(w) = 0. If w ∉ K, then 1_K c(w) = 0 and c(w) = 1_{ℝⁿ∖K} c(w). Since 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1, |b(w)| = χ(w)|b₀(w)| ≤ |b₀(w)| = |1_K c(w) − b₀(w)|, and the triangle inequality gives the bound.
7. (Integration.) Every function in step 6 is integrable on Ω. Indeed, c − b is integrable on Ω since c is integrable on Ω and b is integrable; 1_{ℝⁿ∖K} c is the indicator of a measurable set times c; and 1_K c − b₀ is integrable on ℝⁿ. Integrating step 6 over Ω (`integral_mono`, `integral_add`) gives ∫_Ω |c − b| ≤ ∫_Ω |1_{ℝⁿ∖K} c| + ∫_Ω |1_K c − b₀|. Here ∫_Ω |1_{ℝⁿ∖K} c| = ∫_Ω 1_{ℝⁿ∖K}|c| = ∫_{Ω ∩ (ℝⁿ∖K)} |c| = ∫_{Ω∖K} |c| < δ/2 by step 2 (`norm_indicator_eq_indicator_norm`, `setIntegral_indicator`). And ∫_Ω |1_K c − b₀| ≤ ∫_{ℝⁿ} |1_K c − b₀| ≤ δ/2 by step 3, since the integrand is nonnegative and integrable (`setIntegral_le_integral`). Hence ∫_Ω |c(w) − b(w)| dw < δ/2 + δ/2 = δ. Together with step 5, b has all the required properties. ∎
proof_key_steps: Compact exhaustion K_j = F_j ∩ B̄(0, j) of Ω, where the F_j are closed, increasing, contained in Ω, with union Ω.
By monotone convergence, choose K = K_j with ∫_{Ω∖K} |c| < δ/2.
MemLp.exist_eLpNorm_sub_le with p = 1 gives a C^∞ compactly supported b₀ with ∫ |1_K c − b₀| ≤ δ/2.
Smooth Urysohn cutoff: χ with values in [0, 1], χ = 1 exactly on K, support χ = interior L, where K ⊆ interior L ⊆ L ⊆ Ω and L is compact; b := χ·b₀ is C^∞ with compact support inside Ω.
Pointwise |c − b| ≤ |1_{Kᶜ} c| + |1_K c − b₀|; integrating over Ω gives ∫_Ω |c − b| < δ/2 + δ/2 = δ.

audit.reason: The type exactly states the supported smooth approximation obligation; its explicit smoothness order denotes C∞. The proof supplies the compact exhaustion, strict tail bound, global approximation, smooth cutoff and integrable pointwise majorant. Combining a tail error < δ/2 with approximation error ≤ δ/2 gives the required strict inequality. The resulting field is integrable and C¹, as needed by the parent.

subproblem.title: Convergence of ∫_Ω Du_k(b) against C¹ fields with compact support in Ω
subproblem.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ open, C ≥ 0, and let u : ℝⁿ → ℝ and u_k : ℝⁿ → ℝ (k ∈ ℕ) all be C-Lipschitz on Ω, with u_k → u uniformly on Ω. Then for every C¹ field b : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ with compact support and tsupport b ⊆ Ω, ∫_Ω Du_k(w)(b(w)) dw → ∫_Ω Du(w)(b(w)) dw as k → ∞. Here Df(w) = fderiv ℝ f w (the Fréchet derivative where it exists, 0 otherwise), and integrals are Bochner integrals for Lebesgue measure on ℝⁿ = Eucl n.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (Ω : Set (Eucl n)) (C : ℝ≥0) (u : Eucl n → ℝ) (ug : ℕ → Eucl n → ℝ), IsOpen Ω → LipschitzOnWith C u Ω → (∀ k, LipschitzOnWith C (ug k) Ω) → TendstoUniformlyOn ug u atTop Ω → ∀ b : Eucl n → Eucl n, ContDiff ℝ 1 b → HasCompactSupport b → tsupport b ⊆ Ω → Tendsto (fun k => ∫ w in Ω, fderiv ℝ (ug k) w (b w)) atTop (𝓝 (∫ w in Ω, fderiv ℝ u w (b w)))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions. ℝⁿ = Eucl n; Lⁿ = volume; Df(w) = fderiv ℝ f w (0 where f is not differentiable). Integrals are Bochner integrals for Lⁿ. In Lean the sequence u_k is `ug k`. Source: parent proof, step 5.
1. (Weak divergence of b.) Apply the sibling theorem `slicing_im_ll_gws_lipschitz_ibp` to n, Ω and b; its hypotheses hold because Ω is open, b is C¹ with compact support, and tsupport b ⊆ Ω. It gives g : ℝⁿ → ℝ, Lⁿ-integrable, with the following property: for every L ≥ 0 and every f that is L-Lipschitz on Ω, f·g is integrable on Ω and ∫_Ω Df(w)(b(w)) dw = −∫_Ω f(w)g(w) dw. Apply this with (L, f) = (C, u) and with (L, f) = (C, u_k) for every k; all of these functions are C-Lipschitz on Ω by hypothesis.
2. (Difference formula.) For every k, u·g and u_k·g are integrable on Ω by step 1. By step 1 and linearity of the integral (`integral_sub`), ∫_Ω Du_k(w)(b(w)) dw − ∫_Ω Du(w)(b(w)) dw = −∫_Ω u_k g + ∫_Ω u g = ∫_Ω (u(w) − u_k(w))·g(w) dw.
3. (Choice of N.) Put A := ∫_Ω |g(w)| dw ≥ 0, which is finite because g is integrable and hence integrable on Ω. Let ε > 0 and η := ε/(2(A + 1)) > 0. Since u_k → u uniformly on Ω (`Metric.tendstoUniformlyOn_iff`), there is N ∈ ℕ with |u(w) − u_k(w)| < η for all k ≥ N and all w ∈ Ω.
4. (Estimate.) Let k ≥ N. For all w ∈ Ω, |(u(w) − u_k(w))·g(w)| ≤ η|g(w)|, and η|g| is integrable on Ω. Hence |∫_Ω (u − u_k) g| ≤ ∫_Ω η|g| = ηA = εA/(2(A + 1)) < ε (`norm_integral_le_of_norm_le`, `integral_const_mul`).
5. (Conclusion.) By steps 2 and 4, |∫_Ω Du_k(w)(b(w)) dw − ∫_Ω Du(w)(b(w)) dw| < ε for all k ≥ N. Since ε > 0 was arbitrary, ∫_Ω Du_k(b) → ∫_Ω Du(b) as k → ∞ (`Metric.tendsto_atTop`). ∎
proof_key_steps: The sibling slicing_im_ll_gws_lipschitz_ibp gives one integrable g with f·g integrable on Ω and ∫_Ω Df(b) = −∫_Ω f g, for f = u and for f = u_k.
By uniform convergence, |u − u_k| < η on Ω for k ≥ N, so |∫_Ω (u − u_k) g| ≤ η∫_Ω |g| < ε.

audit.reason: The prose and type agree. The proof uses only its declared sibling lipschitz_ibp, obtaining the same g for u and every ug k. Product integrability justifies subtraction, and uniform convergence with η = ε/(2(A+1)) proves the limit without a finite-measure assumption. There is no reliance on the parent theorem.
